assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: full opaque 16:9 theatrical stage-curtain background texture for an original 1930s cel-adventure game's title screen. Create a SINGLE 2048x1152 landscape image showing a CLOSED scarlet/burgundy velvet theatre curtain, straight-on orthographic flat front view, FULL BLEED cloth from all four edges, broad softly painted vertical hanging folds, restrained antique warm-gold lower hem at the bottom 5 percent, gently scalloped heavy bottom edge but opaque to image boundary. NO opening, NO stage, NO scenery visible, NO rods, NO ties, NO lettering, NO logo, NO characters, NO furniture, NO frame/border, NO decorative emblems. This one complete sheet will rise as a rigid authored UI curtain revealing the main menu beneath; the top must continue beyond the screen, not show a valance or theatre architecture. Match Theatrical Cel Adventure guide: simple broad readable painted shapes, rich muted scarlet #D9363E in lit fold ridges, deep burgundy shadows toward ink #292522, minimal soft grain, painterly scenic support rather than glossy 3D rendering. Keep large center region calm enough for a cream game logo and a bright green cartoon dragon placed later. Slightly darker upper corners, discreet warm light from below; no spotlight painted into image. Original art, no copied recognizable franchise features. Opaque background, high quality finished painted game asset.
assets.note: Final curtain uses the separately recorded alpha cutout; see generated-art.json.

assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: mission entrance icon APPROVAL SAMPLE BOARD only for an original 1930s theatrical cel-adventure game. Create a clean landscape 3-column by 3-row grid on quiet warm ivory paper #eee4ce, with generous spacing and only three short column headings at top: 'A  BUBBLE', 'B  TICKET', 'C  INK'. Rows show identical mission states across the three design families: first row AVAILABLE, second row LOCKED, third row CLEARED. Small left-side state labels verbatim 'AVAILABLE', 'LOCKED', 'CLEARED'. Nine icons total, one per grid cell, all same practical small-game-marker scale and visual weight, with enough empty margin to extract them as sample sprites. A family: irregular hand-inked cream soap-bubble medallion with one simple central state glyph. B family: compact cream punched theatre admission ticket silhouette, slightly oblique but completely flat ink/cel, central state glyph, one clipped corner and a simple punched edge; NO writing, numbers, filigree or tiny detail inside tickets. C family: bare thick hand-inked state glyph with subtle cream outer contour and no medallion/container. Available glyph is a bold friendly exclamation mark in royal blue #1748A5 and ink #292522. Locked glyph is a simple closed padlock in muted warm charcoal/stone, not shiny metal. Cleared glyph is a confident check mark in bottle green #2D6C42 and ink #292522. Shape as well as color must distinguish all states. Match Theatrical Cel Adventure art guide: broad readable silhouettes, strong chunky irregular dark outlines, limited flat cel fills, quiet warm cream support, one saturated focal accent, a hint of handmade line irregularity. These markers must remain legible when eventually reduced to about 24-32 screen pixels. They will sit above existing painted mission entrances; no geometry pin, no drop-pin tail, no flag, no pennant, no particles, no beams, no glowing effects, no modern app UI, no glossy 3D, no maps, no scenery, no characters, no brand logos. The board is a restrained polished original game art comparison, not decorative illustration.
